reviewed-card-sha256-algorithm: plain sha256 over the card file bytes at 80fdccc (git blob fb8b41dce02aa32c573ca9a393d2e4b027f89c07; the working-tree file hashes identically, tree clean). NOT the CE canonical digest: the card sits in tasks/doing/ and declares no blocks:, so ce task validate never reaches the quality-review-receipt check and prints no canonical digest. Same situation as the TASK-382 and TASK-386 receipts.
digest-scope-warning: Because this is a plain file digest and not the CE canonical digest, it also covers the quality-review-receipt: line itself. When the author adds that pointer to this card, the file bytes change and this digest no longer matches the card as committed. That is inherent to the fallback and is why the algorithm field above is explicit; the digest pins what was reviewed (80fdccc), not what is finally committed.
receipt-path-note: This receipt lives at the durable path this very card introduces: tasks/receipts/<TASK-ID>/done-review-<reviewed-card-sha256>.json, git-tracked, not under the gitignored tmp/.

residual-findings.text: The criterion 'tmp/가 없는 체크아웃에서 validate 실패가 6에서 2로 줄고, 남은 2건은 TASK-344·371이다' is marked [x] but its binding is `ce task validate --all`, which exits 1 (88 valid / 2 invalid). The criterion's substance is true and I verified it; the binding, however, does not exit 0 and does not itself assert either the count or the identity of the two survivors — a reader running it sees a failure, not a confirmation. This is the same defect class review-386 recorded as F1 against TASK-386, where a [x] box carried `ce task validate --all` and was narrowed. I did not raise it in rounds 1-3; that is my miss, not a regression introduced in round 4.
residual-findings.status: open, non-blocking — does not change the pass verdict
residual-findings.rationale: the board-wide binding is genuinely informative here (the card is about the board-wide failure count), so simply deleting it would lose information. It is the [x] + exit 1 combination that is wrong.
better-forms-if-ever-wanted: test "$(ce task validate --all 2>&1 | /usr/bin/grep -c '❌ Invalid')" = 2   — exits 0, asserts the count

test "$(ce task validate --all 2>&1 | /usr/bin/grep -B3 '❌ Invalid' | /usr/bin/grep -c 'Validating: tasks/done/\(344\|371\)-')" = 2   — exits 0, asserts the identity of both survivors, which is what the criterion actually claims
